s: The UGC Promotion of Equity in HEIs Regulations, 2026, covering SCs, STs and OBCs, align with which Articles?
x: The regulations align with Articles 15(4) and 15(5); OBCs were excluded only in the draft.

s: In which year was the University Education Commission headed by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan set up?
x: The University Education Commission dates to 1948, after the Sargeant Report (1944) and the committee for Aligarh, Banaras and Delhi universities (1945).

s: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article and from which year?
x: The Election Commission of India is established under Article 324 and dates from 1950. The alternatives alter either the constitutional Article or the year of establishment.

s: The UGC Promotion of Equity in HEIs Regulations, 2026, notified to address caste-based discrimination, replaced which earlier regulations?
x: The 2026 regulations replaced the 2012 regulations. The other years are incorrect because the earlier regulations replaced by the new framework were from 2012.

s: How often must the Equity Committee meet at least under the UGC Equity Regulations, 2026?
x: The Equity Committee must meet at least twice a year, not once.

s: Which provision of the draft was dropped from the final UGC Equity Regulations, 2026?
o: Equal Opportunity Centre in every HEI
Annual equity compliance report to the UGC
Equity Committee chaired by the Head of Institution
Fine on students for false complaints

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The NCW is a statutory body set up in 1992 under the NCW Act, 1990
The NCST is a constitutional body under Article 338A
The NCST was established on 19 February 2004
The previous ECI National Conference of State Election Commissions was held in 2000
x: The previous ECI conference was held in 1999, not 2000.

s: Who inaugurated the UGC in 1953?
x: The UGC, established in 1952, was inaugurated by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad in 1953 and became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956.

s: From which Article does the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes derive its constitutional status?
x: NCST is provided under Article 338A. Article 338 relates to NCSC, Article 338B to NCBC and Article 280 to the Finance Commission.

s: Which of the following bodies is statutory rather than constitutional?
x: NCW was set up under the NCW Act, 1990; the others are constitutional.

s: What is the nature of the Law Commission of India?
o: Non-statutory body set up by government notification
Statutory body under an Act of 1990
x: The Law Commission is executive (non-statutory), set up by notification with terms of reference.

s: Who chairs the 23rd Law Commission of India?
x: Justice Dinesh Maheshwari chairs it; Hitesh Jain and D.P. Verma are full-time members.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?
x: Vijaya Rahatkar chairs the NCW; Antar Singh Arya chairs the NCST.

s: The ECI's National Conference of State Election Commissions in February 2026 was the first since which year?
x: It was the first such conference in about 27 years, the last being in 1999.

s: What did the Sargeant Report of 1944 recommend setting up?
x: The 1944 Sargeant Report recommended a University Grants Committee.

s: In which year did the UGC, established in 1952, become a statutory body?
x: The UGC became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956.

s: Who is the chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Antar Singh Arya chairs the NCST, a constitutional body under Article 338A.

s: What is the term of the 23rd Law Commission of India?
x: The 23rd Law Commission has a three-year term from 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2027.

s: What is the motto of the University Grants Commission?
x: The UGC motto, 'Gyan-Vigyan Vimuktaye', means 'Knowledge Liberates' and appears in its logo.

s: Who was the Chief Election Commissioner at the ECI's National Conference of State Election Commissions in February 2026?
x: CEC Gyanesh Kumar held the conference on 24 February 2026 with ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

s: The Thorat Committee (2007) is associated with which issue?
x: The Thorat Committee (2007) looked into caste discrimination against SC/ST students and is cited for the UGC equity rules.

s: What weight does income distance carry in the 16th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution criteria?
x: Income distance has 42.5%, 2011 population 17.5% and demographic performance 10%.

s: Which of the following was NOT a horizontal devolution criterion of the 15th Finance Commission?
x: Contribution to GDP is the new criterion added by the 16th FC; the 15th FC used demographic performance, forest and ecology, and tax and fiscal effort.

s: Who chaired the 16th Finance Commission, whose report covered the award period 2026–2031?
x: Arvind Panagariya chaired the 16th Finance Commission, whose award period was 2026–2031. N.K. Singh chaired the 15th Finance Commission, while Y.V. Reddy and Vijay Kelkar chaired the 14th and 13th Finance Commissions respectively.

s: Which horizontal devolution criterion was removed by the 16th Finance Commission when 'contribution to GDP' was newly added?
x: The tax and fiscal effort criterion was removed and contribution to GDP was added.

s: The 16th Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41%; what share had the States demanded?
x: States demanded 50%, but the 16th FC retained the 41% share.

s: In what ratio are local body grants split between basic and performance grants under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Local body grants have an 80% basic and 20% performance structure; 90:10 is the disaster-cost sharing for NE and Himalayan states.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 16th Finance Commission's fiscal recommendations?
o: States should cap their fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP
The Centre's fiscal deficit should be 4% of GDP by 2030–31
x: The Centre's target is 3.5% of GDP by 2030–31, not 4%.

s: At what level did the 16th Finance Commission (award period 2026-31) keep vertical devolution to States?
x: Vertical devolution was kept at 41%; a new contribution-to-GDP criterion with 10% weight was added.

s: On which date was the report of the 16th Finance Commission tabled in the Lok Sabha?
x: The 16th Finance Commission report was tabled in the Lok Sabha on 1 February 2026.

s: Which grants were dropped in the 16th Finance Commission award, drawing criticism that it placed efficiency above equity?
x: Revenue-deficit grants were dropped and the income-distance weight was reduced.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Inter-State Council?
x: Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council; Article 280 is the Finance Commission.

s: On which date was the 16th Finance Commission constituted?
x: It was constituted on 31 December 2023; members were notified on 30 January 2024.

s: Population growth during which period is the basis of the 16th Finance Commission's demographic performance criterion?
x: Demographic performance uses population growth 1971–2011, not TFR.

s: Which change did the 16th Finance Commission make to the forest and ecology criterion?
x: The forest criterion kept its 10% weight but now includes open forests.

s: What is the disaster cost-sharing ratio between the Centre and North-Eastern and Himalayan States under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: NE and Himalayan States share 90:10; other States 75:25.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 16th Finance Commission award?
o: The government accepted the 41% vertical share
Tax and fiscal effort was retained as a criterion
Local body grants are split 80:20 basic to performance
x: Tax and fiscal effort was removed by the 16th FC.

s: Why did the divisible pool's share of gross tax revenue fall from 89.1% in 2014-15?
x: Cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, so their rise shrank it to about 74–80%.

s: Which Finance Commission raised the States' share of the divisible pool from 32% to 42%?
x: The 14th Finance Commission under Y.V. Reddy raised the States' share from 32% to 42%.

s: Who was the chairman of the First Finance Commission?
x: The 1st Finance Commission (1951) was chaired by K.C. Neogy.

x: Population's weight was raised to 17.5%; income distance has 42.5%.

s: Which State government set up the Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations?
x: The Tamil Nadu (DMK) government set up the Rajamannar Committee in 1969 to study Centre-State relations.

s: Which body did the Rajamannar Committee want set up at once under Article 263?
x: The Rajamannar Committee called for the immediate setting up of the Inter-State Council under Article 263.

s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up under Article 263?

s: Who was the chairman of the 14th Finance Commission?

s: Who chaired the committee on Centre-State relations set up by the Tamil Nadu Government in 1969?
x: Dr P.V. Rajamannar, a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, chaired this State-level committee.

s: In India's counter-terrorism policy PRAHAAR, CBRNED stands for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, Explosive and what?
x: PRAHAAR defines CBRNED as Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, Explosive and Digital.

s: On which date did the Ministry of Home Affairs release PRAHAAR, India's first national counter-terrorism policy?
x: PRAHAAR was released on 23 February 2026 and has seven pillars, including Prevention and Recovery and resilience.

s: Under PRAHAAR, India’s national counter-terrorism policy, what does the zero-tolerance approach seek to deny terrorists?
o: Crypto funding, dark web access and cyber-attacks by nation-states
x: PRAHAAR’s zero-tolerance approach seeks to deny terrorists funds, weapons and safe havens. Power, railways and aviation are critical sectors, while the other options refer to separate threat categories or manifestations identified in the policy.

s: What position does PRAHAAR adopt regarding the relationship between terrorism and social or civilisational identities?
o: It links terrorism to civilisation but not to religion or ethnicity.
It links terrorism exclusively to one religion.
It links terrorism to ethnicity but not to religion or civilisation.
It does not link terrorism to any religion, ethnicity or civilisation.
x: PRAHAAR does not link terrorism to any religion, ethnicity or civilisation. The other options introduce identity-based linkages that the policy explicitly avoids.

s: NATGRID has been integrated with which database for population-scale surveillance?
x: NATGRID was expanded into population-scale surveillance and integrated with the NPR.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NATGRID?
o: It handles tens of thousands of queries a month, including from state police
Its analytical tools include entity resolution, facial recognition and machine learning
It originated as a response to the 2001 Parliament attack
It engages the right to privacy recognised in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017)
x: NATGRID originated as a response to the 26/11 Mumbai attacks in 2008.

s: What was the distinguishing national-level feature of NIDMS, launched by the Ministry of Home Affairs in January 2026?
o: India's first national IED data platform
India's first digital creators' content platform
x: NIDMS was India's first national IED data platform and was built by the National Bomb Data Centre of the NSG. The other options describe land data, digital creators' content or legal services rather than IED data.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PRAHAAR?
o: It recognises cyber-attacks by nation-states as a threat
It recognises crypto funding as a terrorism-related threat
It treats cyber-attacks as terrorism only when carried out by non-state actors
It recognises the dark web as a terrorism-related threat
x: PRAHAAR specifically recognises cyber-attacks by nation-states, so limiting it to non-state actors is wrong.

s: How many pillars does PRAHAAR, India's national counter-terrorism policy, have?
x: PRAHAAR rests on seven pillars, from Prevention to Recovery and resilience.

s: Which body built NIDMS, India's first national IED data platform?
o: National Bomb Data Centre of the NSG
Ministry of Home Affairs' LWE Division
x: NIDMS was built by the National Bomb Data Centre (NSG) and launched at Manesar.

s: NATGRID was conceived as a response to which event?
x: NATGRID originated after 26/11 to integrate fragmented intelligence databases.

s: On what basis are funds allocated under the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority?
x: FNTA funds are based on population and area; the Mini-Secretariat is headed by a senior officer.

s: The Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority has powers over how many subjects?
x: The Authority has powers over 46 subjects, including land use, agriculture, rural development and infrastructure.

s: Which Article, concerning Nagaland's customary law, remains intact under the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority agreement?
x: Article 371(A) remains intact; the Authority covers Kiphire, Longleng, Mon, Noklak, Shamator and Tuensang.

s: The tripartite agreement creating the institutional framework for eastern Nagaland was signed on 5 February 2026 among which parties?
o: The Centre, the Rajya Sabha and the Nagaland Government
The Centre, the Manipur Government and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation
The Nagaland Government, the Hill Areas Committee and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation
The Centre, the Nagaland Government and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation
x: The agreement was tripartite among the Centre, the Nagaland Government and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation. The Hill Areas Committee is associated with a similar model in Manipur, not with the three-party agreement.

s: Which district is NOT part of the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority?
x: FNTA covers Kiphire, Longleng, Mon, Noklak, Shamator and Tuensang; Dimapur is excluded.

s: Under which Article does the Hill Areas Committee of Manipur, a model similar to FNTA, function?
x: The Hill Areas Committee is under Article 371(C); 371(A) concerns Nagaland.

s: In which year did Nagaland become a State?
x: Nagaland became a State in 1963; ENPO later demanded a separate Frontier Nagaland State.

s: Which hill range separates Manipur and Nagaland?
x: The Barail range separates Manipur and Nagaland.

s: Why were questions on PM CARES, PMNRF and the National Defence Fund held inadmissible in the Lok Sabha?
o: They involve voluntary contributions and are not financed from the Consolidated Fund of India.
They are financed from the Consolidated Fund of India.
They are constitutional courts rather than funds.
They were created only for displaced persons after Partition.
x: The PMO informed the Lok Sabha Secretariat that these funds involve voluntary contributions and are not financed from the Consolidated Fund of India. The displaced-persons-after-Partition description applies to PMNRF, while the other options do not state the reason for inadmissibility.

s: In 2020, to which fund did the Supreme Court refuse to transfer PM CARES money?
x: The SC refused the transfer of PM CARES money to the NDRF; CAG audit applies to the NDRF, not PM CARES.

s: Which Parliamentary Friendship Group is correctly matched with its chair?
x: Shashi Tharoor chairs the France group. USA is chaired by Baijayant Panda, Israel by Ravi Shankar Prasad and Japan by Manish Tewari.

s: Each Parliamentary Friendship Group formed by Speaker Om Birla has how many members?
x: Groups were formed with 64 countries, each having 11 members.

s: Who chairs the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025?
x: Speaker Om Birla appointed Aparajita Sarangi to chair the 31-member JPC.

s: What does the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, referred to a JPC, concern?
o: Removal of PM, CMs and Ministers held in custody
x: The Bill and two related Bills deal with removal of PM/CMs/Ministers held in custody.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM CARES?
o: It is a 'public authority' under the RTI Act
It was set up on 27 March 2020
It is a public charitable trust
It is not financed from the Consolidated Fund of India
x: PM CARES is not a public authority under RTI.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: PM CARES – Set up on 27 March 2020 as a public charitable trust
PMNRF – For displaced persons after Partition
National Defence Fund – Welfare of the armed forces
PM CARES – A “public authority” under RTI
x: PM CARES is not a “public authority” under the RTI Act; the other pairs are correct.

s: In which year was the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) set up?
x: PMNRF was set up in 1948 to help displaced persons after Partition; PM CARES dates from 2020.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ad hoc judges in High Courts?
o: Ad hoc judges are appointed under Article 224A
Articles 214–231 deal with the Supreme Court
Their number is capped at 10% of the sanctioned strength
Retired High Court judges may serve as ad hoc judges
x: Articles 214–231 concern the High Courts, not the Supreme Court.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise the Public Trust Doctrine, which originated in Roman law?
o: M.C. Mehta vs Union of India (1987)
x: The Supreme Court recognised the Public Trust Doctrine in M.C. Mehta vs Kamal Nath (1997).

s: Justice Lisa Gill was recommended as Chief Justice of which High Court?
x: The SC collegium recommended Justice Lisa Gill for the AP High Court and Justice Suresh Aravind for Madras.

s: How many of the 25 High Courts appointed ad hoc judges after the Supreme Court permitted them under Article 224A?
x: None of the 25 High Courts acted on the permission.

s: Which provision provides for disqualification for promoting enmity?
o: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
x: RPA Section 8 covers disqualification for promoting enmity; BNS 353 covers incitement endangering public order.

s: What did the Bezbaruah Committee of 2014 deal with?
x: The Bezbaruah Committee dealt with racial and regional discrimination; mob lynching guidelines came from Tehseen Poonawalla (2018).

s: What was the key distinction of the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025?
o: Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law on untouchability
Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law only on hate speech
Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law only on hate crimes
Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law on hate speech and hate crimes
x: Karnataka was the first State to bring a dedicated law on hate speech and hate crimes. The tempting alternatives narrow its scope to only hate speech or only hate crimes, whereas the Bill covers both.

s: In which case was Section 66A of the IT Act struck down?
x: Section 66A was struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015).

s: What major legal gap was highlighted in connection with the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025?
o: India has no provision for disqualification for promoting enmity
India has no provision dealing with untouchability
India has no law on mob lynching guidelines
India has no statutory definition of hate speech
x: The highlighted gap was that India has no statutory definition of hate speech. The other options refer to subjects dealt with under other legal provisions or judicial guidelines, not the specific gap identified.

s: Under the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, on whom does collective liability for hate speech linked to an organisation fall?
o: Only the person making the speech
Only the publisher of the content
x: The Bill provides for collective liability of office-bearers of linked organisations.

s: What does the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025 empower the State to do about online hateful content?
o: Only refer such content to the Centre
Only seek court orders for removal
x: The Bill empowers the State to block or remove hateful online content.

s: Which new Sections did Law Commission Report 267 (2017) on hate speech propose?
x: Law Commission Report 267 (2017) proposed new Sections 153C and 505A.

s: In Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan (2014), what did the Supreme Court ask the Law Commission to do?
x: The SC asked the Law Commission to define hate speech; mob lynching guidelines came in Tehseen Poonawalla.

s: What did the Viswanathan Committee (2015) deal with?
x: The Viswanathan Committee dealt with identity-based offences; Bezbaruah with racial discrimination.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court issue guidelines against mob lynching?
x: Tehseen Poonawalla (2018) laid down guidelines on mob lynching.

s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaces IPC Section 153A on promoting enmity between groups?
x: BNS Section 196 is the former IPC 153A; Section 299 is the former 295A.

s: Census 2027 is to include caste enumeration for the first time since which Census?
x: Caste enumeration returns for the first time since 1931; the Census is conducted by the RGCC under the MHA.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a commission on backward classes?
x: Article 340 provides for a commission on backward classes.

s: In which year was the Criminal Tribes Act, which labelled tribes as 'born criminals', enacted?
x: The Criminal Tribes Act dates from 1871; 1872 and 1881 are census years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 8th Economic Census proposed for 2027?
o: It will help build a Statistical Business Register
It covers establishments meant solely for personal consumption
The NSO conducts it with State Directorates of Economics & Statistics
x: The Economic Census covers establishments producing or distributing goods and services, except those meant solely for personal consumption.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026–27 Population Census?
o: It will be the first fully digital Census with self-enumeration.
It will be the 15th decennial Census.
It will have a separate head for transgender-headed households.
Its first phase (House Listing) runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026.
x: It will be the 16th decennial Census, not the 15th.

s: Which sequence correctly describes the planned Population Census and 8th Economic Census?
o: 8th Economic Census in 2026 followed by Population Census in 2027
Population Census in 2026–27 followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2027
Population Census in 2027 followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2026–27
Both censuses will be conducted simultaneously in 2026–27
x: The two-phase Population Census is scheduled for 2026–27, followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2027. The other options reverse or incorrectly merge the sequence.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about census and backward-class provisions?
o: The Registrar General & Census Commissioner functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Census is placed in Entry 69 of the Concurrent List
The Census Act, 1948 keeps individual census data confidential
Article 340 provides for a commission on backward classes
x: Census is in Entry 69 of the Union List, not the Concurrent List.

s: Which of the following census year – milestone pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1921 – First complete census of a city
x: 1881 saw the first synchronous census. 1830 was the first complete city census, 1872 the first all-India non-synchronous census and 1921 the Great Divide.

s: Who conducts the Census of India?
o: Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under MHA
x: The RGI under the Ministry of Home Affairs conducts the Census.

s: Under whom was India's first synchronous census of 1881 conducted?
x: 1881 was the first synchronous census under Plowden; 1872 (Mayo) was non-synchronous.

s: What is the name of the unified enterprise database that the 8th Economic Census aims to build?
x: The 8th Economic Census will build a Statistical Business Register.

s: In which year was the first Economic Census held in India?
x: The first Economic Census was held in 1977; the 8th is due in 2027.

s: Under which Viceroy was the first all-India, non-synchronous Census held in 1872?
x: The 1872 Census was held under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous Census was in 1881.

s: Under which Act is the Census of India conducted?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
x: The Census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, which keeps individual data confidential.

s: Which Census year is known as the 'Great Divide' because India's population declined that decade?
x: The 1921 Census showed the only decadal decline (-0.31%), linked to the 1918 influenza.

s: Who conducted the first complete census of a city, Dacca, in 1830?
x: Henry Walter carried out the 1830 census of Dacca, the first complete census of a city.

s: Which High Court upheld the Bihar caste survey in 2023?
x: The Patna High Court upheld the Bihar caste survey in 2023; the Supreme Court issued notice.

s: Which distinction is associated with the Salal Hydroelectric Project in the context of the Indus Waters Treaty framework?
o: It was the first rural road project in Mandi district
It was the first vertical-lift sea railway bridge in India
It was India’s first coal-to-SNG project
It was the first hydropower project built by India in Kashmir under the IWT framework
x: Salal was the first hydropower project built by India in Kashmir under the Indus Waters Treaty framework. The vertical-lift bridge, coal-to-SNG project and rural road are separate developments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the airport monetisation model and sector outlook?
o: The model shifted from revenue-sharing to a per-passenger fee, with tariffs regulated by AERA
AERA may impose tariff cuts up to 10% for missing service benchmarks
Only 6% of Indians fly, and 50 new airports are planned in five years
The airport network is expected to reach 163 airports
x: AERA penalties can include tariff cuts of up to 5%, not 10%.

s: According to the NITI Aayog report on end-of-life vehicles, what was the operating condition of most vehicle-scrapping centres?
x: Most vehicle-scrapping centres were operating below 20% of their capacity. The alternatives change the reported level of utilisation and therefore do not reflect the finding of the report.

s: Who launched Bharat Taxi, India's first cooperative ride-hailing platform, on 5 February 2026?
x: Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched Bharat Taxi; Rekha Gupta was linked to Delhi's partnership with it.

s: Bharat Taxi is described as India's first what?
x: Bharat Taxi is described as the first cooperative ride-hailing platform.

s: Which State/UT became the first to partner with Bharat Taxi?
x: Delhi was first, via an MoU between DTTDC and Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Ltd in the presence of CM Rekha Gupta.

s: What measure did the Union Power Minister direct at the Salal Hydroelectric Project amid the Indus Waters Treaty being in abeyance?
x: The Union Power Minister directed sediment flushing at the Salal Hydroelectric Project. The project began construction in 1970, entered commercial operation in 1987, and provides 12.5% of its power to J&K; these are associated facts, not the directed measure.

s: Who launched National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, the second phase of asset monetisation of brownfield infrastructure?
x: Nirmala Sitharaman launched National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0. Shivraj Singh Chouhan launched Bharat-VISTAAR, while Amit Shah launched Vibrant Villages Programme-II.

s: What happens to ownership and revenue rights under National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, which supports the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
o: Ownership remains with the government while revenue rights are leased
Ownership is transferred while the government keeps revenue rights
Both ownership and revenue rights are sold
x: Under NMP 2.0 government ownership is retained while revenue rights are leased.

s: Which group of sectors was covered under the first National Monetisation Pipeline launched in 2021?
o: Roads, railways, power transmission and ports
Roads, railways, power transmission and airports
Roads, railways, power transmission, airports and ports
x: The first National Monetisation Pipeline was launched in 2021 and covered roads, railways, power transmission, airports and ports. The most tempting alternative omits ports, which was one of the sectors included.

s: Bharat Taxi signed a Memorandum of Understanding for regulated airport taxis with which organisation?
x: Bharat Taxi signed an MoU with the Airports Authority of India (AAI) for regulated airport taxis. Delhi Traffic Police, DMRC and SBI were other partners associated with Bharat Taxi, but they were not identified for this airport-taxi MoU.

s: What is the key feature of the third round of airport privatisation proposed by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in January 2026?
o: Sale of six AAI airports to a single operator
Lease of 11 AAI airports under PPP
Lease of 50 new airports under PPP
x: The third round proposes leasing 11 Airports Authority of India airports under a public-private partnership, with the proposal sent to PPPAC. A major first in this round is the bundling of metro and non-metro airports into five bundles; it is not a sale of six airports to one operator.

s: Which airports were privatised in 2003?
x: Delhi and Mumbai were privatised in 2003; Hyderabad and Bengaluru were greenfield BOOT projects.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Monetisation Pipeline?
o: NMP 2.0 transfers ownership of assets to private players
x: Under monetisation, ownership stays with the government; only revenue rights are leased.

s: Who prepared National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0?
x: NMP 2.0 was prepared by NITI Aayog; it is monitored by a Core Group chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.

s: To what does the revenue-sharing model shift in the third round of airport PPP?
x: The model shifts from revenue-sharing to a per-passenger fee.

s: Who chairs the Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation that monitors National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0?
x: The Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.

s: What was the monetisation target of the first National Monetisation Pipeline for FY22-25?
x: NMP 1.0 (2021) aimed at ₹6 lakh crore over FY22-25 and achieved 88.3%.

s: What is the size of National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 for FY2026-30?
x: NMP 2.0, prepared by NITI Aayog, is worth Rs 16.72 lakh crore; NMP 1.0 (2021) had a target of Rs 6 lakh crore.

s: In which year was the Union Ministry of Cooperation set up?
x: The Ministry of Cooperation was created in 2021; its minister Amit Shah launched Bharat Taxi.

s: What is the vector of lymphatic filariasis?
x: Culex quinquefasciatus is the vector of lymphatic filariasis.

s: According to the World Malaria Report 2025, to what level did malaria cases in the Asia-Pacific region fall from 9.6 million in 2023?
x: Cases fell from 9.6 million to 8.9 million, with 10 of 17 endemic countries recording declines, making the region a bright spot.

s: Which is the most severe type of spina bifida?
x: Myelomeningocele is the most severe type; folic acid in early pregnancy helps prevent spina bifida.

s: Which malaria vaccines are prioritised for Africa?
x: The malaria vaccines identified are RTS,S and R21, not BCG and OPV.

s: Which pair of Plasmodium species is identified as the principal malaria species in India?
x: India mainly has P. falciparum and P. vivax. P. malariae and P. ovale are also malaria species, but they are not the pair identified as mainly prevalent in India.

s: Who launched the Lymphatic Filariasis Mass Drug Administration programme in February 2026, which targets elimination by 2027?
x: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda launched the LF MDA programme with a 2027 elimination target.

s: By which year does India aim to achieve zero indigenous malaria cases?
x: India's target is 2027; 2030 is the global target.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Plasmodium is a protozoan, not a bacterium; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-RAHAT?
o: ERSS-112 integration lets a victim call 112
The grievance officer is appointed by the State Road Safety Committee
Stabilisation is for 24 hours in non-critical and 48 hours in critical cases
Reimbursement is from the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund under Section 164B of the MV Act, 1988
x: The grievance officer is appointed by the District Road Safety Committee, not the State committee.

s: Under PM-RAHAT, what cashless treatment cover is available to each road accident victim?
o: Up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for 48 hours
Up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for 24 hours
Up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for 7 days
Up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for 3–5 years
x: PM-RAHAT provides cashless treatment cover of up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for 7 days from the accident. The other options give treatment periods that do not match the scheme’s stated coverage period.

s: Who unveiled the 'Uday' mascot in January 2026?
x: The Uday mascot was unveiled by UIDAI, not MoSPI.

s: What reward does a helper receive under the Rah-Veer (Good Samaritan) Scheme?
x: The reward is ₹25,000; the scheme is under Section 134A of the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019.

s: What does PM-RAHAT, the scheme launched by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in 2026 for road accident victims, stand for?
o: Road Safety Hospitalisation and Accident Trauma Support
Road Emergency Support and Health Assistance for Traffic
Road Accident Victim Relief and Hospital Assistance for Treatment
Road Accident Victim Hospitalization and Assured Treatment

s: Which PFRDA committee was assigned to review NPS investment guidelines and submit its report in nine months?
x: The Narayan Ramachandran Committee was tasked with reviewing NPS investment guidelines and submitting its report in nine months. The M. S. Sahoo Committee dealt with a guaranteed and predictable pension under NPS.

s: Where was the pilot of the GIS-based Land Stack platform undertaken?
x: The Land Stack pilot was run in Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu; it was launched in New Delhi.

s:

Reason (R): PANCHAM uses Bhashini for its 22-language support.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

A is false, but R is true

s: With what is cellulitis, a bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue, treated?
x: Cellulitis is caused by bacteria such as Streptococcus and Staphylococcus and is treated with antibiotics.

s: What was the PFRDA's M.S. Sahoo Committee set up to examine?
o: An assured pension under the NPS
x: M.S. Sahoo deals with assured pension; Narayan Ramachandran with investment guidelines.

x: Lymphatic filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti and spread by Culex quinquefasciatus.

s: Which agency runs the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)?
x: PMBJP is run by the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI, 2010) under the Chemicals and Fertilizers ministry.

s: Which body launched Sampurnata Abhiyan 2.0 for saturation in Aspirational Districts and Blocks?
x: NITI Aayog ran Sampurnata Abhiyan 2.0 (28 Jan to 14 Apr 2026) in 112 Aspirational Districts and 513 Blocks.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the PFRDA?
x: PFRDA (est. 2003, Act 2013) is chaired by Sivasubramanian Ramann; Tuhin Kanta Pandey heads SEBI.

s: How many Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks are covered by NITI Aayog's Sampurnata Abhiyan 2.0?
x: Sampurnata Abhiyan 2.0 (28 Jan-14 Apr 2026) aims at 100% saturation in 112 Aspirational Districts and 513 Aspirational Blocks.

s: For which region is Karna-18, a salinity- and drought-tolerant sugarcane variety reported in January 2026, intended?
x: Karna-18 is tolerant to salinity and drought and is intended for north-western India.

s: According to the Bank of Baroda report based on CMIE data, which State ranked first in investment attraction during the first nine months of 2025–26?

s: According to the Bank of Baroda report on investment attraction in 2025–26, which State ranked second?
x: Andhra Pradesh was first (25.3%) and Odisha second (13.1%).

s: Which State was the top State in organ donation under Jeevandan 2025?
x: Telangana's Jeevandan recorded 763 transplants from 205 donors in 2025, the top State.

s: Root wilt disease of coconut is caused by which of the following?
x: Root wilt is caused by a phytoplasma in the phloem; first identified at Erattupetta, Kerala.

s: From which institution was Telangana's Manmohan Singh Earth Sciences University upgraded?
x: The university was upgraded from the Kothagudem School of Mines (1978) and got statutory status in 2026.

s: Who chairs the 8th Central Pay Commission?
x: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th Central Pay Commission.

s: Which item in the 8th Central Pay Commission's Terms of Reference signals concern about a return to the Old Pension Scheme?
o: The cost of the Unified Pension Scheme
The funded cost of contributory pension schemes
The unfunded cost of non-contributory pension schemes
The unfunded cost of market annuity schemes

s: From which date are the recommendations of the 8th Central Pay Commission to be effective?
x: The 8th CPC recommendations are effective from 1 January 2026; its report is due in 18 months.

s: Who chaired the 7th Central Pay Commission?
x: Ashok Kumar Mathur chaired the 7th CPC; Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th.

s: Within how many months must the 8th Central Pay Commission submit its report?
x: The report is due within 18 months.

s: Under which department of the Finance Ministry does the 8th Central Pay Commission work?
x: The 8th CPC is a non-statutory advisory body under the Department of Expenditure.

s: What is the employee's contribution under the Unified Pension Scheme?
x: The UPS employee share is 10%; 14% is the government share in the NPS.

s: What type of scheme is the Unified Pension Scheme, effective from 1 April 2025 with an assured payout?
x: UPS is hybrid, whereas NPS is defined contribution.

o: UPS – 50% of last basic plus DA
NPS – 50% of last basic plus DA

s: Under the NPS, what share of the corpus can be withdrawn tax-free at retirement?
x: 60% is withdrawn tax-free and 40% goes to annuity.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about pension schemes?
o: The NPS for government employees began in 2005
Employees contribute under the Unified Pension Scheme
The UPS became effective from 1 April 2025
The choice of the UPS is irreversible
x: The NPS for government employees began in 2004, not 2005.

s: To which scheme did the Finance Ministry permit Central government employees a one-time, one-way switch from the Unified Pension Scheme?
x: The permitted switch was back to NPS, not to OPS.

s: The Unified Pension Scheme carries the same Income Tax Act, 1961 benefits as which scheme?
x: UPS has the same income-tax benefits as NPS, not OPS.

s: Which group of States was identified as having returned to the Old Pension Scheme?
o: Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Kerala and Rajasthan
Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh
x: The identified States are Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. The other options replace one or more of these States with States not included in the stated group.

s: What is the minimum pension under the Old Pension Scheme?
x: OPS minimum is ₹9,000; ₹10,000 is the UPS minimum.

s: On whose recommendations was the Unified Pension Scheme based?
x: UPS came from the T.V. Somanathan Committee.

s: What is the government's contribution under the Unified Pension Scheme?
x: Government share is 18.5% under UPS; 14% is under NPS.

s: What is the minimum pension under the Unified Pension Scheme for 10 or more years of service?
x: UPS assures a minimum pension of ₹10,000; ₹9,000 is the OPS minimum.

s: To which price index is the Unified Pension Scheme indexed?
x: UPS, from the T.V. Somanathan Committee, is indexed to CPI-IW.

s: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, what is the assured pension for 25 years of service?
o: 50% of last basic pay plus DA
60% of average basic pay of the last 10 months
50% of average basic pay of the last 12 months
x: UPS gives 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years' service; OPS gave 50% of last basic plus DA.

s: On which product was a high-risk cess, earmarked for cancer care, recommended?
x: A high-risk cess on tobacco was recommended, with its proceeds earmarked for cancer care.

s: The National Cancer Registry Programme covers about what share of India’s population?
x: It covers only 18% of the population; the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions (163rd report) recommended making cancer notifiable.

s: Under the present WHO norm, cited in the proposal to make cancer notifiable, which diseases are notifiable?
x: At present only communicable diseases are notifiable; the cancer proposal would extend this.

s: The proposal to declare cancer a notifiable disease was linked with which programme and SDG?
x: The linked programme is NPCDCS and the goal is SDG 3.

s: On which date did the 16th Finance Commission submit its report to President Droupadi Murmu?
x: It was submitted on 17 November 2025, within the extended tenure.

s: Under which Article does a Finance Commission report become public when tabled in Parliament?
x: Article 281 covers laying the report before Parliament; Article 280 sets up the Commission.

s: What was the subject of Law Commission Report No. 279?
o: Usage of the Law of Sedition
Age of Consent under POCSO Act
x: Report 279 (2023) concerned sedition.

s: Which Law Commission report dealt with simultaneous elections?
x: Simultaneous elections were the 170th report (1999); 279th was on sedition.

s: Which of the following pairs (Law Commission report – subject) is correctly matched?
x: 285 is criminal defamation; 279 is sedition, 283 POCSO consent age and 289 trade secrets.

s: Who chaired the 22nd Law Commission?
x: Ritu Raj Awasthi chaired the 22nd; Dinesh Maheshwari chairs the 23rd.

s: Which committee recommended declaring cancer a notifiable disease?
x: The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions did so in its 163rd report.

x: Narain Dass Gupta heads the committee.

s: How many members does the JPC on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 have?
x: It is a 31-member JPC chaired by Aparajita Sarangi.

s: Which Law Commission report dealt with the age of consent under the POCSO Act, 2012?

s: According to NCRB 2023 data, illness, the second-largest cause of suicides after family problems, accounted for what share?
x: Illness accounted for 19% of suicides, second after family problems (32%).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NCRB 2023 data on atrocities against SCs and STs?
o: Cases against STs numbered 12,960, an increase of 18.8%.
Cases against SCs numbered 57,789, an increase of 0.4%.
Over 60% of PoA cases were pending, per the National Campaign on Dalit Human Rights.
The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in 1989.

x: Myrdal coined the 'soft state'; Dumont is linked to the purity-pollution hierarchy.

x: Abortions are governed by the MTP Act.

x: Tamil Nadu had 21%, ahead of Maharashtra (12%) and Karnataka (10%).

x: Family problems caused 32% of suicides, followed by illness at 19% (ADSI 2023).

x: Louis Dumont explained caste through purity and pollution; Gunnar Myrdal gave the 'soft state' idea.

s: Under SEBI’s proposed governance reforms for Market Infrastructure Institutions, which vertical must be headed by an Executive Director?
x: Critical Operations is a mandatory vertical headed by an Executive Director. Commercial Interests and Business Development was a vertical where an Executive Director was at the MII’s discretion, not a mandatory requirement.

s: Under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, seed traceability requires onboarding on which portal?
x: Traceability requires onboarding on the SATHI Portal, along with mandatory QR code labelling.

s: Which Ministry prepared the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
x: The Draft Seeds Bill, 2025 was prepared by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The other ministries are related to economic and regulatory functions but were not identified as the ministry for this Bill.

s: The Draft Seeds Bill, 2025 seeks to replace which existing instruments?
o: Agricultural Produce Act, 1966 and Seeds Order, 1983
x: The Bill seeks to replace the Seeds Act, 1966 and the Seeds (Control) Order, 1983. The other combinations alter the titles or years of the instruments.

s: Under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Seeds sold in the market – Three-year provisional registration
Varieties notified under the Seeds Act, 1966 – Deemed registered
x: Varieties notified under the 1966 Act are deemed registered; market seeds need VCU-based registration, existing varieties get three-year provisional registration, and VCU means Value for Cultivation and Use.

s: Under which system are multi-state seed firms deemed registered under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025?
x: Multi-state firms are deemed registered under the Central Accreditation System; unregistered imported varieties are allowed only for research or trials.

s: A concern about the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, including GM seed risk, is that VCU testing can be done by whom?
x: Foreign entities can conduct VCU testing, raising concerns such as GM seed risk; seed banks, FPOs and women collectives may also be treated as commercial units.

s: Up to what value may Vice-Chancellors and directors approve global tenders under the June 2025 changes to the General Financial Rules?
x: The approval ceiling for global tenders is ₹200 crore; the direct purchase limit rose from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh.

s: Who is associated with the concept of mission-oriented procurement?
x: Mission-oriented procurement is associated with Mariana Mazzucato.

s: Which of the following pairs (country – procurement model) is correctly matched?
x: South Korea is linked to pre-commercial procurement; Germany to High-Tech Strategy and KOINNO, the USA to SBIR and the EU to the Joint Procurement Agreement.

s: By about how much are the draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 expected to cut test licence applications?
x: The expected cut is about 50%; processing time falls from 90 to 45 days.

s: Under SEBI’s proposed governance reforms for Market Infrastructure Institutions, what minimum number of Executive Directors must each MII have?
x: SEBI proposed at least two Executive Directors for each Market Infrastructure Institution, reporting to the Managing Director. The other numbers are not the minimum proposed under the reform.

s: Under SEBI's proposed MII reforms, who may hold non-executive posts in unlisted government companies or not-for-profits?
x: MDs may hold such posts; EDs may hold none except in MII subsidiaries.

s: Under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, farmers may sell farm-saved seed, but in which way may they not sell it?
x: Farmers may save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed, but not under a brand name.

s: To what amount was the direct purchase limit raised from ₹1 lakh under the June 2025 GFR reforms?
x: The limit was raised to ₹2 lakh, not ₹5 lakh.

s: Under the draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, the processing time is cut from 90 days to how many days?
x: The draft cuts processing time from 90 to 45 days and replaces most test licences with intimation to the CLA.

s: What is the maximum fine for major offences such as selling spurious or unregistered seeds under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025?
x: Minor offences carry up to ₹2 lakh; major offences up to ₹30 lakh, with cancellation or imprisonment.

s: Which body is the drug regulator under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019?
x: CDSCO is the regulator; the draft amendments replace the test licence with intimation to the Central Licensing Authority.

s: India's tiger population, cited in the Tribal Affairs Ministry's conservation policy, rose from about 1,411 in 2006 to over how many in 2023?
x: Tigers increased from about 1,411 in 2006 to over 3,000 in 2023.

s: Under the UK's Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, 2024, whose approval was required?
x: The Bill required High Court approval, not Supreme Court approval, and excluded mental illness and disability.

s: Under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ policy for tiger reserves, relocation, an exceptional last resort, cannot take place until the process under which law is complete?
x: Relocation is a last resort and cannot happen before the Forest Rights Act process is complete.

s: What framework was proposed under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ new policy on community-centred conservation in tiger reserves?
o: National Framework for Tiger Protection and Relocation
National Framework for Community-Centred Conservation and Relocation
National Framework for Tribal Welfare and Rehabilitation
National Framework for Community-Centred Forest Development
x: The proposed framework is the National Framework for Community-Centred Conservation and Relocation. The other options alter the stated title and do not refer to the proposed framework.

s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338A) was set up in 2004 through which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The NCST was created by the 89th Amendment; Article 275(1) separately provides grants for ST welfare.

s: In January 2025, the Supreme Court directed whom to frame a comprehensive law for domestic workers and form an expert committee within six months?
x: The direction was to the Centre, not the States; the Domestic Workers Bill, 2017 was never enacted.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about measures relating to domestic workers in India?
o: Karnataka’s Domestic Workers Bill, 2025 proposes a 5% employee contribution to the welfare fund
India has not ratified ILO Convention No. 189
Tamil Nadu’s Welfare Board under the Manual Workers Act, 1982 has a wage rate of ₹37–39 per hour
India voted for ILO Convention No. 189 in 2011
x: Karnataka’s Bill proposes a 5% employer contribution, not an employee contribution.

s: Under which Article did the Supreme Court in 2018 recognise the right to die with dignity and allow passive euthanasia?
x: The right to die with dignity was recognised under Article 21.

s: Which Article of the Constitution defines Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 366(25) defines STs; Article 342 lets the President specify them.

s: Which earlier directive did the Ministry of Tribal Affairs' policy on community-centred conservation in tiger reserves overturn?
o: The 2024 NTCA directive for mass removal of villages
x: The MoTA policy makes relocation a last resort and overturns the 2024 NTCA directive for mass removal of villages.

s: Which ILO Convention on domestic workers has India voted for but not ratified?
x: India voted for ILO Convention C189 (2011) on domestic workers but has not ratified it.

s: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution applies to tribal areas in which States?
o: Meghalaya, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides grants-in-aid from the Union for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes?

s: In which year was the Ministry of Tribal Affairs set up?
x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up in 1999.

s: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are implemented through which body?
x: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs are run through TRIFED.

s: The Union Health Ministry’s recommendations on organ transplantation included mandatory data sharing with which organisation?
x: The recommendation was mandatory data sharing with NOTTO. Co-WIN and U-WIN are immunisation platforms, while DigiLocker is used for the CBSE marksheet facility.

s: Which country's model does India's front-of-pack labelling to fight non-communicable diseases follow?
x: Front-of-pack labelling follows the Singapore model, not Thailand's.

s: How many kidney transplants did India record in 2024–25, against a demand of over one lakh?
x: India recorded 13,476 kidney transplants in 2024–25 against demand of over one lakh.

s: With which chemical was Coldrif cough syrup, linked to the deaths of at least 16 children in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, contaminated?
x: The syrup contained diethylene glycol, confirmed by the Tamil Nadu Drugs Control laboratory; CDSCO recommended cancelling the licence.

s: After the Coldrif cough syrup deaths, the Health Ministry stressed compliance with which requirement?
o: Revised Schedule M on Good Manufacturing Practices
x: The Health Ministry stressed strict compliance with revised Schedule M on Good Manufacturing Practices.

s: In which country did a diethylene glycol cough-syrup incident kill over 60 children in 2022?
x: The 2022 incident was in Gambia; the 2023 incident was in Uzbekistan.

s: Which development is highlighted as part of the triple burden of malnutrition in India?
x: The triple burden of malnutrition includes the trend of obesity overtaking underweight. The alternatives reverse or exaggerate the reported development.

s: According to UNICEF India, non-communicable diseases cause what share of deaths in India?
x: NCDs cause 63% of deaths in India; 25–26% refers to premature NCD deaths.

o: A two-year-old girl from Palnadu district
A two-year-old boy from Palnadu district
A two-year-old girl from Guntur district
A five-year-old girl from Palnadu district

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the human H5N1 death in Andhra Pradesh?

Infection was confirmed on 31 March by NIV, Pune.
The child's contacts tested positive for H5N1.

s: Which statement correctly describes H5N1 in the context of the reported Andhra Pradesh case?

It is a low-pathogenic avian influenza, and human-to-human transmission is confirmed
It is a form of leptospirosis, and human-to-human transmission is confirmed
It is a bacterial respiratory infection, and human-to-human transmission remains unconfirmed

Submergence in Chhattisgarh was studied by the Central Water Commission.
